Added a dedicated color/time legend above the timeline slider so users can see exactly which hues map to oldest vs. newest points, using the same normalized color ramp as the map markers. Introduced a shared helper for the history hue gradient and localized the legend label (en/de/ja).

```895:960:miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceHistoryMapView.swift
private struct TimelineColorScale: View {
    let range: ClosedRange<Double>
    let ticks: [Double]

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
            Text(NSLocalizedString("history_timeline_color_scale_label",
                                   comment: "Label describing the timeline color-to-time mapping"))
                .font(.caption2)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let width = geometry.size.width
                ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: gradientColors,
                                             startPoint: .leading,
                                             endPoint: .trailing))
                        .frame(height: 10)

                    ForEach(ticks, id: \.self) { tick in
                        let x = position(for: tick, width: width)
                        Rectangle()
                            .fill(Color.primary.opacity(0.24))
                            .frame(width: 1, height: 14)
                            .offset(x: x - 0.5, y: -2)
                            .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    }
                }
            }
            .frame(height: 18)

            HStack {
                Text(formattedLabel(for: range.lowerBound))
                Spacer()
                Text(formattedLabel(for: range.upperBound))
            }
            .font(.caption2)
            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
    }
}
```

**Explaining gradient behavior in timeline slider**

The gradient on the entire track uses a fixed color mapping across the full range, and the selection overlay applies the same gradient mask without rescaling colors to the selected region, so colors correspond to absolute timeline positions rather than relative selection. If desired, the gradient could be re-anchored to scale colors within the selection bounds, but currently it reflects the global range.</details></think>

---

Currently the gradient is applied to both the whole track and the selected region mask. The colors are not re-scaled to the selection; they remain anchored to the full timeline range. That means the selection simply shows the corresponding slice of the overall blue→red ramp (older→newer) rather than recomputing a new gradient for just the selected span.

max(minDelta, (maxLat - minLat) * 1.4)\n            let paddedLon = max(minDelta, (maxLon - minLon) * 1.4)\n            let latitudeDelta = paddedLat.isFinite ? paddedLat : minDelta\n            let
